name: Broccoli haircut

card.summary: A voluminous, forward-combed mop of hair, shorter on the sides, that adds fullness and softens the forehead.

quick.overview:
The broccoli haircut is a style with a thick, rounded top that falls toward the forehead and is cut shorter at the sides, giving a mushroom-like outline. It is used to add volume and frame the face.

The term is common in gym and style conversation, where it describes a trend among younger men. No studies cover it; what exists is informal commentary.
quick.how: It is typically cut with length on top and trimmed sides, then styled forward with a comb and sometimes a styling product. Men with thick hair are described as the best fit for the shape.
quick.risks: There are no health risks. One commenter speculates that thick hair plastered to the forehead could be uncomfortable.

lead: The broccoli haircut is a nickname for a voluminous top that curves forward over the forehead, resembling the head of a broccoli floret. It is sometimes called the Korean broccoli cut.
Gym forum users use the term in passing, usually when describing a popular look among younger lifters.[1][2]

chain: Long, thick top with shorter sides
Fullness and a fringe frame the forehead
Face looks softer and hair looks denser
angle.text: The cut concentrates length on top, so it shows off hair density and covers part of the forehead. It depends on having enough hair.

paras: T Nation posters describe the cut as a thick head of hair combed forward to the eyebrows.[3] Others mention it in passing as a trend seen among young gym-goers.[1][2]
